inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities and lease principal repayment are IMMATERIAL for Napier Port (lease liability balance NZ$26k / repayment of lease liabilities NZ$270k FY2025, i.e. thousands, not the CSV's millions scale) -- no owner-FCF adjustment required and no lease debt added to net debt. This differs from the port/keiretsu names in this folder that carry material IFRS-16 books; verified against the FY2025 10-K note 14 (Loans and borrowings, NZ$109.65m, which excludes the trivial lease liability) and the financing-activities cash flow line.
inputs.notes: Model: Owner-FCF DCF (component build), section 7 non-US/cyclical adaptations applied. Napier Port is an operating infrastructure company (regional-monopoly container/bulk/cruise port), not a REIT/bank/LIC, so the owner-FCF engine is the correct route per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md. Fresh build -- no prior NPH.NZ DCF exists (checked research/NPH.NZ/Reports/NPH.NZ_DCF.json, absent; ticker also absent from MEMORY.md). 10-year explicit horizon used because the FY2025-27 $120m Napier Port Transformation programme + $36m Port Otago dredge JV keeps capex well above D&A (currently ~2.7x) through FY2027, so year-1 to year-3 owner-FCF margins (2-13%) are far below the mature ~23% margin reached only once capex normalizes toward maintenance levels from FY2028 -- a 5-year Gordon capitalization would freeze an immature, capex-depressed margin in perpetuity. SBC and IFRS-16 leases are both genuinely immaterial for this filer (verified in filings, not assumed) -- see sbc_source and lease_treatment above. Interest income not stripped: Napier Port is a NET-DEBT company (net debt NZ$129.5m at 31-Mar-2026), not net-cash, so there is no cash pile to double-count; net finance costs (NZ$5.4m FY2025) are already inside NPAT/reported FCF as a cost and are not separately added to the bridge. Cyclone Gabrielle (Feb-2023) insurance recovery income (NZ$8.9m FY2024, NZ$7.5m FY2025, now fully and finally settled per FY2025 10-K note 5) is booked in 'Other (income) and expenses', BELOW the 'Result from operating activities' / EBITDA line used as this model's revenue-EBITDA-margin anchor -- confirmed by direct extraction of the FY2023-25 income statements, so the historical EBITDA-margin series used to calibrate the base case (31.5% FY2023 trough to 40.7% FY2025) is a clean operating recovery, not an insurance-income artifact. FY2023 margin trough reflects genuine cost inflation ahead of yield-management repricing, not an accounting one-off.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.9-4.3%) diverges sharply from revenue CAGR (9.5-11.3%) and EPS CAGR (6.4-14.5%) -- more than 30% relative divergence. This is a capex-driven divergence, not an earnings-quality problem: Napier Port has been funding the $120m NPT programme substantially through debt and retained earnings while paying out a large share of NPAT as dividends (FY2025 total 14.5cps incl. a 2.5c special vs EPS 15c), so book value compounds far slower than revenue/earnings even though the underlying business is genuinely growing. The DCF growth path is therefore driven by the component build calibrated to FY2026 guidance and the post-NPT margin trajectory, not by the equity CAGR mechanically.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are not meaningful on the reported series: FY2021-22 FCF was deeply negative (-$68.9m / -$39.0m) from the initial container-terminal capex programme, and FY2023 flipped positive as that programme wound down, so a CAGR formula on a sign-changing series is undefined. The owner-FCF adjustment (SBC deduction only, ~0.16% of revenue) makes negligible difference to the reported series given SBC's immateriality here -- unlike the US-tech names in this folder, there is no material gap between reported and owner FCF for NPH.NZ.

base.narrative: FY2026 revenue growth (7.5%) anchored to the reaffirmed $70-74m underlying result-from-operating-activities guidance (H1-2026 actual $37.3m annualizes to the guidance band) and the H1-2026 trading update (containerised volumes up on horticulture/MSC Eagle service, bulk/log down on geopolitical pressures). EBITDA margin recovers from the FY2023 Cyclone Gabrielle-era trough (31.5%) through the FY2025 level (40.7%) toward a mature 44.5% as yield management (avg revenue/TEU +12.8% H1-2026) and NPT productivity gains land. Capex stays elevated (32%, 30%, 22% of revenue) through FY2026-28 to fund the $120m NPT programme (FY2025-27) plus the $36m dredge JV, then normalizes to a ~12% maintenance-plus-modest-growth level once the transformation programme completes and D&A on the newly capitalized base rises to absorb it. Revenue growth decelerates from 7.5% to a 3% long-run rate reflecting a mature regional-monopoly hinterland with modest volume upside from Port Plus+ logistics extension.

bull.narrative: NPT and the dredge JV deliver on schedule and under budget: capex tapers faster (to ~11% of revenue by FY2029 vs base's ~13%) as the $120m programme completes cleanly by FY2027 without overrun, autonomous-truck productivity plus the 14.5m channel depth lift throughput capacity materially, yield management continues compounding (avg revenue/TEU/tonne gains persist), and Port Plus+ (Viewpoint, Manawatu Inland Port JV) adds a genuine second growth leg beyond the wharf. Record apple exports and Pan Pac's return to full production continue the post-cyclone recovery into sustained above-trend volume growth. Margin matures at 47.5%, above the FY2025 actual, reflecting full operating leverage on the expanded asset base.

bear.narrative: The NPT programme runs over budget and over schedule (capex stays above 20% of revenue through FY2029 rather than normalizing by FY2028), cost inflation (flagged by management as a near-term risk) outpaces the yield-management repricing that rescued the FY2023 margin trough, and log/bulk export volumes stay structurally weak on 'geopolitical pressures and higher costs' (already visible in the nine-month FY2026 update: bulk down 4.6% YoY). Cruise continues its structural decline (calls down ~30% in H1-2026) with no offset. HBRIC/Council majority ownership constrains capital-allocation flexibility (e.g. dividend policy prioritized over debt paydown) in a downturn. Owner FCF is negative in years 1-2 as elevated capex meets a compressed, slow-recovering margin -- a real near-term cash-flow risk, not a modelling artifact -- before the transformation capex tapers from year 3.

bear.flags: Owner FCF is negative in FY2026-27 (years 1-2) under this scenario as elevated NPT/dredge capex meets a margin still stuck near the FY2023 trough. Terminal value is NOT floored at zero -- year-10 owner FCF recovers to a modestly positive $38.9m as capex normalizes even in the bear case, so the scenario represents a slower, costlier recovery rather than a going-concern outcome. Flagged per method section 4 because interim cash flow is genuinely negative for two years, which is itself a real risk (covenant headroom, dividend sustainability) worth calling out even though it does not force the zero floor.

base.entry_price_correction_note: Terminal value rebuilt at the hurdle rate 2026-09-01: min(Gordon@hurdle, cap x FCF_N). The superseded value held the WACC-built terminal value and varied only the discounting.

entry_price.note: The 15% hurdle sits well above the base-case WACC (8.35%), so entry prices land materially below intrinsic value across all three scenarios -- consistent with the method's sanity check (growth well below 15% implies entry price meaningfully under IV, not merely 'modestly below' it). The gap is wide here because NPH.NZ's near-term owner FCF is compressed (and negative in the bear case) by the FY2025-27 capex supercycle, so the interim cash flows a 15%-hurdle buyer collects in years 1-3 are small; most of the entry-price support comes from the terminal value even at the punitive 15% discount rate.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's required return (min(Gordon@r, cap x FCF_N)), so the flows and the exit are charged the same rate. Corrected 2026-09-01.

sensitivity.note: Terminal-growth range is base-case terminal growth (2.5%) +/-1pp in 0.5pp steps, per section 7(a). At the two lowest WACC rows the Gordon terminal value exceeds the 20x cap and the cap binds, flattening several cells at the capped value (3.90 / 3.53) -- this is the cap doing its job (section 4), not a calculation error.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear weight set above the 15% house default (to 20%) because Napier Port carries real, near-term, evidenced downside risk beyond generic cyclicality: single-site concentration proven by Cyclone Gabrielle, a $120m+dredge capex programme that could overrun into a higher-for-longer rate environment, log/bulk volumes already softening on 'geopolitical pressures and higher costs' per the nine-month FY2026 update, a structurally declining cruise segment (-30% calls H1-2026), and a majority government owner (HBRIC/Council ~55%) whose capital-allocation priorities may not track pure commercial logic in a downturn. Bull weight trimmed to 30% (vs 35% default) because the bull case requires several things to go right simultaneously (NPT on-time/on-budget, dredge JV timeline held, yield management gains persisting, Port Plus+ scaling) rather than one dominant lever. Base holds the default 50%.
probability_weighted.band_position_note: SBC is genuinely immaterial for Napier Port (~0.16% of revenue, verified in the FY2025 10-K -- see inputs.sbc_source). Per section 7(e), the house/street band therefore collapses to a single point rather than reporting a degenerate band_position of 0%; house and street intrinsic values are identical in every scenario.

historical_multiples.source: 10-year monthly Yahoo Finance closes (NPH.NZ, IPO Aug-2019), aligned to the closest trading day to each 30-September fiscal year-end
historical_multiples.note: At the current $3.62 price the stock trades at ~11.9x FY2026 guidance-midpoint EBITDA (result from operating activities $72m) and ~13.3x FY2025 actual -- squarely inside its own 5-year post-IPO-hype trading range (10.9x-17.4x, excluding the FY2019 IPO-year outlier at 8.8x), not at an extreme. This supports the 20x EV/FCF-equivalent terminal cap used in the base case (roughly consistent with a mid-teens EV/EBITDA multiple once the FCF/EBITDA conversion ratio at maturity, ~53%, is applied) and indicates the market is pricing NPH.NZ as a normal, moderately-growing regulated-monopoly-style infrastructure asset rather than assuming either distress or a re-rating.

sanity_checks: Owner FCF ~= reported FCF for NPH.NZ (SBC and lease adjustments both immaterial, verified in filings) -- unlike most tickers in this folder, the SBC/lease corrections make negligible difference here; the valuation swing versus a naive DCF is almost entirely in the component margin build (capex supercycle) and WACC, not the SBC/interest adjustments.
Cyclone Gabrielle insurance recoveries (FY2024/25) confirmed booked BELOW the EBITDA line used in this model -- historical EBITDA margin series used for calibration is clean of that one-off.

FY2026 guidance cross-check: H1-2026 result from operating activities $37.277m annualizes consistently with the reaffirmed $70-74m FY2026 guidance range (implied H2 of $32.7-36.7m vs H1's $37.3m, a plausible seasonal split).
Bear-case terminal value NOT hitting the zero floor -- flagged and explained in valuation.bear.flags.

Weighted IV (NZ$3.06) sits between the base (NZ$2.87) and bull (NZ$4.62) cases, pulled up from base by the 30% bull weight and bull's meaningfully higher IV (+61% vs base) even after trimming bull's weight below the 35% default -- bear's severe -68% downside is dampened in the blend by its lower 20% weight. This is the expected shape given a base/bull/bear IV ordering of 2.87/4.62/1.20 and 50/30/20 weights.
quality_flags.weighted_iv_recompute_check: 0.20*1.1992 + 0.50*2.8704 + 0.30*4.6161 = 0.23984 + 1.4352 + 1.38483 = 3.05987, matching probability_weighted.weighted_iv (3.06) to rounding. Uses full-precision per-scenario IVs (bear 1.1992, base 2.8704, bull 4.6161); the 2dp figures shown in valuation.* are for display only.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (SBC ~0.16% of revenue, so adjusted and GAAP multiples are indistinguishable for NPH.NZ); FY-end = September close; price history starts at the Aug-2019 IPO so the window is 7 FYs, not 10.
sanity_check.outlier_rationale: FY2019 is the IPO year: weighted-average share count (120.6m) understates the 200m post-float count and NPAT carries one-off listing costs, giving a meaningless 51x P/E.
sanity_check.conclusion: Passed: base IV $2.87 implies 19.3x P/E, 1.35x P/B and 11.0x EV/EBITDA, all at or BELOW what the market has historically paid (avg 26.3x / 1.51x / 14.9x). The negative base-case upside is the market paying a monopoly-infrastructure premium above a 15%-hurdle owner-FCF value, not an over-aggressive model.
